statement: Whenever reorder_log_files returns a result r, it satisfies the following. Let n = len(logs). For a log x, let id(x) be the byte string before its first space and body(x) be the byte string after its first space. Let L be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n such that logs[i] is a letter-log. Then len(r) = n; the multiset of entries r[0],...,r[L-1] is exactly the multiset of all letter-logs in logs; for every k with 0 <= k < L, r[k] is a letter-log; for every k with L <= k < n, r[k] is a digit-log; for all i,j with 0 <= i < j < L, either body(r[i]) <_lex body(r[j]), or body(r[i]) = body(r[j]) and id(r[i]) <=_lex id(r[j]); and the sequence r[L],...,r[n-1] is exactly the sequence of digit-logs of logs in their original order, i.e. logs[j] for j in increasing order such that logs[j] is a digit-log. Here <_lex and <=_lex denote standard byte-wise lexicographic order.
preconditions: logs is a non-empty slice of byte-vector strings with 1 <= len(logs) <= 100; each log has length between 3 and 100; each log consists of an identifier followed by a single space and at least one word, with tokens separated by single spaces; for each log, every non-identifier word consists entirely of lowercase English letters (a-z) or entirely of digits (0-9), and all non-identifier words of that log are of the same kind. Thus each log is either a letter-log or a digit-log.
